messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@fairview.bank>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2029 09:17:00 -0500
Subject: RFI: Fairview Bank SIG - Telemetry & Dataflow Evidence

Irene,

Thanks for taking this — Fairview is running through the SIG v2 and we have a tight window to validate telemetry and dataflow controls for our procurement committee. Two specific asks where we need clarity and sample artifacts: 

1) Telemetry retention & redaction: we need to understand what fields Redwood retains in request/telemetry logs (timestamps, request_id/correlation, user identifiers, prompt text, generated output) and whether you can provide redacted samples that preserve auditability (timestamps + request_id) but remove PII or prompt content.

2) Control mapping: please map the SIG questions (Network/Logging/Monitoring, Data Handling) to specific Redwood controls/artifacts and indicate owner + expected artifact name.

Attached the SIG spreadsheet our team is using (Fairview_SIG_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm if redacted telemetry is acceptable for attestation purposes and provide an ETA for sample artifacts? Our target decision window is Jan 26.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morris
Senior Information Security Analyst 
Fairview Bank

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2029 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Fairview Bank SIG - Telemetry & Dataflow Evidence

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Short answers up front: yes, redacted telemetry samples are acceptable for the SIG review provided they retain immutable audit fields (UTC timestamps, request_id/correlation_id, model/version identifier) and are accompanied by a short attestation describing the redaction process and hash of the original log batch we retained for audit. 

Proposed artifact list and ETA: 
- control-mapping-fv.csv — mapping of SIG question -> Redwood control, owner, artifact name (Karthik will own) — ETA Jan 18
- redacted-telemetry-sample.jsonl — newline-delimited JSON, timestamps & request_id preserved; prompt/output redacted with deterministic token-hash — ETA Jan 17 (Hannah)
- SOC2-snapshot-2028Q4.pdf — excerpted report pages for logging/monitoring — sent by end of day Jan 15

If that works, we will deliver the redacted sample and mapping, plus a short text attestation. One clarification: do you need raw prompts removed entirely, or can we provide hashed prompt fingerprints (sha256) so your PO can validate uniqueness without seeing content?

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Team — looping you both in to confirm owners and approach. High-level plan below; please reply with acceptance/edits.

Scope: Fairview wants SIG v2 answers plus evidence demonstrating telemetry retention, ability to redact, and proof of auditability. They explicitly called out timestamps and request_id preservation.

Owners & actions: 
- Karthik: produce control-mapping-fv.csv mapping SIG rows to our controls (control id, short description, artifact filename, owner contact, retention statement). Target Jan 18. Format: CSV w/ columns [SIG_row, control_ref, artifact, owner, notes].
- Hannah: generate a sanitized telemetry sample (redacted-telemetry-sample.jsonl). Requirements: newline JSON entries with fields preserved for timestamp (iso8601), request_id, model, and hashed_prompt (sha256 hex) instead of raw prompt; full output can be redacted to "<REDACTED>" but indicate token-count. Also include a small manifest file with original file hash for audit. Target Jan 17.
- Irene: pull SOC2 pages and draft a short attestation describing redaction/hash process; coordinate upload to shared Drive and provide link for Fairview. Target Jan 15.

Compliance note: Legal suggested including a short line that sample data was derived from a synthetic run and not customer data; if Fairview requires production-sourced logs for audit, escalate to Legal — but prefer synthetic plus hash of retained batch for chain-of-custody.

Please confirm and flag any blockers.

Thanks — Irene

Irene — quick follow-up. Two clarifications from our procurement reviewers: 

1) Redaction fidelity: acceptable if timestamps and request_id are preserved, but they also want continuity of request flow (i.e., parent_request_id present if request was a follow-up) so we can verify causal chains.

2) Hashing prompts: acceptable provided we receive the hashing algorithm and salt policy so we can reproduce the fingerprinting in our validation environment. Can you confirm you will provide the salt handling policy and whether salts are per-batch or per-environment?

If you can confirm by Jan 19, we can include this in our committee packet.

Regards,
Elena
